_mode_2_notes: Mode 2 fires when the bolt-4 SCM scanner finds a <whitesource> target in build.xml.
The scanner injects WhitesourceXmlAntTask into the Ant project and executes the target.
Each <module name=X path=Y> element becomes a separate Mend project named X.
Dependencies within each module are flat (no transitive graph) — all JARs on the path are direct deps.
Expected outcome: TWO Mend projects ('module-a' and 'module-b'), each with 3 direct deps.
Fallback outcome (Mode 3): if Mode 2 does not fire, the scanner performs a recursive path scan
across lib/** and emits a SINGLE flat list of all 6 JARs as direct deps of the root project.
The expected-tree.json encodes Mode-2 as the primary expectation via subtrees[].
The _mode3_fallback block documents what Mode-3 output looks like so the comparator
can distinguish 'Mode-2 fired correctly' from 'fell through to Mode-3'.

_mode3_fallback.description: If Mode 2 does not fire, Mend emits a single flat project with all 6 JARs

warnings: Mode-2 detection requires WhitesourceXmlAntTask to be injected by the Mend scanner at runtime.
Running 'ant whitesource' locally fails with 'task whitesource not found' — this is expected.
If Mode-2 does not fire (scanner version mismatch, feature disabled), Mode-3 fallback produces
a single flat project with all 6 JARs rather than two separate module projects.
The comparator should check subtrees[] length: 2 subtrees = Mode-2 fired; 0 subtrees + flat root = Mode-3 fallback.
Ant itself is not pinnable via install-tool — only java is pinned in .whitesource versioning.
This is a partial reproducibility limitation: the Ant runtime version comes from operator install.
